Temperature-independent switching rates in silicon metal–oxide-semiconductor field–effect transistors at low temperatures

the temperature-independent switching rates for the RTSs in a silicon metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor observed at low temperatures are consistent with a crossover between thermal-activation and tunneling.

(1) the switching rate of a random telegraph noise signal in the drain voltage of a Si metal–oxide–semi-conductor field-effect transistor at constant drain current and gate voltage is thermally activated above a crossover temperature of 30 K, and (2) the switching rate is temperature independent below 30 K, which is consistent with the crossover from thermal activation at high temperatures to tunneling at lower temperatures.
